meta.title: slang.ie — For Focal Sake!
meta.subtitle: A 32 County Guide to Irish Slang
meta.note: Curated preview subset (book-touched + multi-county classics). Full corpus plugs in via data/entries.json.

entries.definition: A description of someone involved in horseplay, maggeh being the Dubinese for maggot.
entries.example: "Gerrouradatgarden and stop acting de maggeh ye bleedin' muppeh!"
entries.posh_english: Do remove yourself from the shrubbery and cease behaving like a complete nincompoop!

entries.definition: An expression used in an argument to make light of the issue, literally means, "Ah come on now, be reasonable."
entries.example:
Aul Doll: "Dawddy, will you givvup lyin' up like a brute?"
Aul Boy: "Ahgoway Mawmmy, yer always makin' things a hanlin' hiy! Boys a dear!!!"
entries.posh_english: Father, will you cease reclining about like an absolute brute?

entries.definition: A local abbreviation of aren't I? Used by individuals seeking the endorsement of self-praise, pronounced amment elsewhere.
entries.example: "I'm goin' with yousins for a wee race to the front of the road (shopping area), ampta?"
entries.posh_english: I am accompanying you good people on a brisk constitutional to the high street, am I not?

entries.definition: One's posterior. The 'r' is pronounced very definitely. In Northern counties it is pronounced awrshe.
entries.example: "Me arse is killin me"
entries.posh_english: My posterior is causing me considerable discomfort.

entries.definition: An impolite way of saying no to someone whilst instructing them to feck off. "Go and shyte" is often used as an alternative.
entries.example: "Tell Anto, if he doesn't like me sambos, he can go ask me arse!"
entries.posh_english: Inform Anthony that if my culinary sandwiches do not meet his exacting standards, he can kindly swivel!

entries.definition: An expression often used to precede an arbitrary sentence. Most likely a variant of ach.
entries.example:
"Are ya goin' out tonight?"
"Awk shor we'll see hiy!"
entries.posh_english: Are you planning upon frequenting the town this evening?

entries.definition: Person from the countryside or of an agricultural persuasion. Most likely comes from a mispronunciation of the beagle breed of dog (given its mongrel heritage).
entries.example: "Get up the road ye oul bagel!"
entries.posh_english: Take yourself back up the lane, you antiquated rustic!

entries.definition:
Useless.
Also: Broken or hurt or exhausted.
entries.example:
"Jays the remote is banjaxed!"
"God me leg is banjaxed"
entries.posh_english: Good heavens, the remote control is quite broken.

entries.definition: In a bad state of repair.
entries.example:
"I was banjaxed last night hi led"
"That yoke's banjaxed"
entries.posh_english: I was terribly worse for drink last night, my good fellow.

entries.definition: Broken/damaged beyond repair.
entries.example: "De fuckin' haybob's banjaxed, I'm after hittin' a rock with it in the long acre."
entries.posh_english: The wretched agricultural implement is completely damaged beyond repair after I struck a rock with it in the boundary field.

entries.definition: A collection or mass of filaments growing from the skin in the pubic area. Pubic hair.
entries.example: "Das de hairiest fanta bazz I've ever seen! Did yer mudder knit dat for ya like?"
entries.posh_english: That is the most densely vegetated pubic region I have ever witnessed. Did your maternal parent knit that for you?

entries.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer
entries.definition: Refers to a girl with a bit of meat (mayte) on her bones. In today's world she would be said to have cankles (i.e. can't tell where her calf muscles end and her ankles begin).
entries.example: "Now das the kind of yungwan I'm into, look at her biys, she's beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer!"
entries.posh_english: Now that is precisely the sort of young lady I fancy, look at her chaps, she is rather sturdily proportioned about the ankles!

entries.definition: One of the most overused words in Dublinese. Bleedin' can be placed in front of any word but is generally used in a negative context e.g.
entries.example:
"Ye bleedin sap / muppeh" = You stupid idiot!
"Ye bleedin rat" = Why you informant you!
"Bleedin woegious" = Unbelievably terrible!
entries.posh_english: You utter simpleton!

entries.definition: The home of the rayle (sic) boxty according to Leitrim people (though Cavan and Fermanagh people would disagree). Making boxty is a fine art and if carefully made over a long period it will clean one's digestive system out. Boxty is a type of potato cake made from mashed and grated potatoes mixed with flour. The cakes are boiled and then sliced and fried in butter.
entries.example: "Give the giblet schome bockshty, she's not had a good oul shyte for hershelf in days!"
entries.posh_english: Provide the infant with some potato bread, as she has not achieved a satisfactory evacuation for days.

entries.definition: Can be used to refer to the male testes and scrotum collectively. Can also be used as an affectionate term for a male friend, as in If spelt with an 'ox' it can refer to a person with whom one is totally dissatisfied, such as a
entries.example:
"g'wan ye bollix."
"biased, blind, baldy, bollox of a ref!"
entries.posh_english: Do crack on, you delightful scoundrel.

entries.definition: The gaelic for faecal matter excreted by the body in order to eliminate the waste products of metabolism and other non-useful materials.... otherwise known as shyte.
entries.example:
"Á cac! Tá mo guthán marbh."
(A shyte! Me phone is dead.)
entries.posh_english: Oh rubbish! My mobile telephone has ceased to function.

entries.definition: Having undesirable or negative qualities. Cat is also used in Armagh / Sligo and other areas.
entries.example: "Dat owl ghrroad to Kilkenny is cat dog malojan! Tank feck we're getting a new wan!"
entries.posh_english: That antiquated thoroughfare to Kilkenny is utterly abominable! Thank goodness we are acquiring a replacement.

entries.definition: Slang word for fun, involving alcohol and music. Craic, the gaelicized version is often labelled as faux-Irish as it is not Irish per se. The term is said to originate from Scotland and has been adopted throughout the whole of Ireland without exception. Often used in a greeting as in
entries.example:
"real"
"What's the craic?"
entries.posh_english: What is the prevailing state of amusement?

entries.definition: A tree-hugging, stripey-sock wearing, unshaven hippy, with long dreadlocks under a tea cosy, army surplus clothing and multiple nose piercings. Often spotted queuing for dole.
entries.example: "Ah slur, we'll be here all day with all the crusties around!"
entries.posh_english: Good grief, we shall be detained here indefinitely with all these eccentric environmentalists about the place!

entries.definition: Someone from the countryside, which to the Dubs, is anyone living outside Dublin city. Other general terms to describe culchies include bog-warrior (bogger) and muck-savage.
entries.example: "You are a culchie."
entries.posh_english: You are a rustic provincial.

entries.definition: Someone who is cunning as a fox. Cavan people are often referred to as cute hoors.
entries.example: "Yan fella's a right cute hoor, if he dropped a Euro it would hit him on the back of the neck on the way down to pick it up!"
entries.posh_english: That chap is a singularly cunning rogue. If he happened to drop a coin, it would strike him in the nape of the neck on its descent.

entries.definition: This infectious term originated in Dublin but has since travelled the length and breadth of the country. Can be followed with several words including buzz, rapid and others.
entries.example:
"Did ye hear Ireland got a new manager?"
"Ah deadly buzz!"
entries.posh_english: Did you hear that Ireland has acquired a new manager?

entries.definition: Extremely nice. Most likely comes from the gaelic for nice: deas. Nowadays it has been replaced in many areas by the word deadly, however, it is acceptable to combine the two words together as in "das deadly desh."
entries.example: "That rissole from Burger Mac's was quare tasty. In fact, it was desh!"
entries.posh_english: That deep-fried savoury morsel from the establishment was delightfully toothsome, and quite splendid indeed.

entries.definition: A person who fell out of the ugly tree and hit every branch on the way down.
entries.example: "Ahh lad, dah wan I shifted last night dog rough, she had a head like a boiled bollix!!!"
entries.posh_english: My dear fellow, the lady I cavorted with last night was rather unfortunate of visage, possessing a countenance resembling a boiled potato.

entries.definition:
Something bad, annoying or disappointing.
Also: The opposite of what you might think... in Waterford slang dose means a prolonged bout of illness or a bad case of something, which can include the scutters, bad luck, an annoying person and so on.
entries.example:
"Some dose gettin chucked out of ruby's dudder night boy wasin it?"
"Lads I have piles like a bag of chynees hanging out of me arse, some dose!"
entries.posh_english: What a thoroughly bad business getting thrown out of Rubys the other night, was it not?

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition: To suffer from a bout of flatulence at the expense of one's neighbour.
entries.example: "Did you drop one? I'm scunnered listening to your awrse, quick open de windy!!!"
entries.posh_english: Did you happen to pass wind?

entries.definition: A person that is socially unexciting. With a person such as this, one would rather commit seppuko(Hari-Kari) than converse with them.
entries.example: "You'd swear dat chap had a towel permanently wrapped around his bollix, he's such a dry balls!"
entries.posh_english: You would wager that fellow had a hand towel permanently secured about his nether regions, such is his utter lack of vivacity.

entries.definition: A very plain individual.
entries.example: "Yer wan is fiersche easy to draw, she've a face like a baboon's awrshe."
entries.posh_english: That woman is frightfully plain, possessing a countenance resembling a primate's posterior.

entries.definition: Probably the most overused Irish word, means idiot. Most often used in a derogatory sense.
entries.example: "Ye big half-shit feckin' eejit!"
entries.posh_english: You large, exceedingly unpleasant imbecile!

entries.definition: Another term to describe the male appendage.
entries.example: "I'm bogged to me elder in this shuck (see Cavan, full as a shuck)!"
entries.posh_english: I am terribly incapacitated by drink in this cavernous establishment!

entries.definition: Greeting. shortened version of Well. Often followed with boy (pronounced biy) or girl.
entries.example: "Ell girl, hows it going?"
entries.posh_english: Hullo old girl, how are things proceeding?

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: A non-vulgar replacement for a similar word with a 'u' instead of the 'e'. Like eejit, it is used extensively. Does not have any sexual connotations, i.e. one would not say However, it can be used in most other circumstances. For example, etc.
entries.example:
"I'd like to feck yer wan."
"feck dat,"
"feck off,"
"I will in me feckin' hole!"
entries.posh_english: I should rather like to court that young lady.

entries.definition: A yungfella. Often used in a derogatory manner.
entries.example: "That feen was gee-eyed after drinkin' too many bottles o' Bucky (see Armagh)."
entries.posh_english: That young fellow was thoroughly intoxicated after consuming far too many bottles of poitín.

entries.definition: A wild football bulltoe shot that invariably goes miles wide. Legend has it that the technique was perfected in Fermanagh.
entries.example: "Yer man gave it holly and produced a Fermanagh banana, we're steeped!"
entries.posh_english: That chap struck it with tremendous force and produced a wildly errant trajectory, we are immensely fortunate!

entries.definition:
Very.
Also: Excellent.
entries.example:
"That car is fierce quick."
"You're a fierce soccer player, Mike."
entries.posh_english: That motorcar is remarkably swift.

entries.definition: Very, great.
entries.example:
"She has a fierce arse on her"
"Its fierce cold"
entries.posh_english: She has a very fine posterior on her.

entries.definition: Express extreme like/dislike.
entries.example: "Dat fella was sumthin feirce"
entries.posh_english: That gentleman was something fierce indeed.

entries.definition: A good looking person. Can also mean sexual intercourse.
entries.example: "Jay yer wan is a right fla, unlike her sister who has a face like a well slapped arse!"
entries.posh_english: Good heavens, that young lady is exceptionally attractive, unlike her sister who possesses a face like a severely boxed rump!

entries.definition: Expression used to describe when a female is going through her menstrual cycle.
entries.example: "Sorry luv, not tonight, I'm in me flowers... de pitch, as they say, is well and truly flooded."
entries.posh_english: Pardon me, my dear, not this evening, as I am indisposed with my monthly courses.

entries.definition: An affectionate term for Dungarvan.
entries.example: "Are ye headin' down tew Fraher Field in Fungarvan for de auld match?"
entries.posh_english: Are you gentlemen proceeding down to the sports grounds for the customary fixture?

entries.definition: A home made slingshot/catapult, made out of a coat hanger and a mixed array of elastic bands. Can refer to an elastic band in the singular.
entries.example:
"I got a slap in de eye offa copper bullet fired from me brudder's gallybander and I couldn't see me blaas for a week!"
Ire (n., pronounced eye-er)
A rash induced by rubbing together of skin and wet clothing on the inner thighs / buttocks.
"Yer man must have ire under his arms, his pants are so far up his hole!"
entries.posh_english: I received a severe blow to the ocular region from a metallic missile launched via my brother's catapult.

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition: Alcoholic beverages. Can be used to as an alternative to "going out on the town."
entries.example: "I'm headin' out on de gargle tonight, I'll be gee-eyed and elephants drunk later on!"
entries.posh_english: I am embarking upon a vigorous session of potable indulgence this evening, and shall be thoroughly legless by dawn.

entries.definition: Used to describe someone or something that was funny. For example, or Describing Hitler as a gas man would be neither accurate nor appropriate.
entries.example:
"it was a gas crack"
"he's a gas man."
entries.posh_english: It proved to be a thoroughly comical evening.

entries.definition: The anus / hole, also known as one's hoop. In rhyming slang it is often substituted with Brenda Fricker.
entries.example: "Meet you??? I will in me Brenda Fricker!"
entries.posh_english: Meet you? I shall do so precisely never!

entries.definition: See Fanny. Can also describe the act of horseplay or a person one does not like.
entries.example: "Give up the gowling ye gowl!"
entries.posh_english: Cease your tomfoolery, you absolute nuisance!

entries.definition: In Limerick, this term means someone who is nasty. One is basically comparing the person to the 'c' word (for vagina).
entries.example: "Ah g'wan, gimme a Meanie ye greedy gowl!"
entries.posh_english: Oh, do cease your hesitation and surrender a confectionary morsel, you miserly wretch!

entries.definition:
A girls private parts.
Also: Vagina, also used as a verb to get up to mischief, to joke, mess, take the piss in a friendly way.
Also: Female genitalia.
entries.example:
"Awwill give her sum kik in de gowl in a minute if she dnt shut up"
"I was only gowlin witcha boy"
"Give up the gowling ya gowlbag."
entries.posh_english: I will give her a kick in the vagina in a moment if she does not shut up.

entries.definition: Good, of acceptable quality.
entries.example: "It'd be grand if you could please pass the salt."
entries.posh_english: It would be good if you could please pass the salt.

entries.definition: In replacement of good Carlow people tend to say Grand.
entries.example: "It's a grand old day int it?"
entries.posh_english: It is a perfectly splendid old day is it not?

entries.definition: Opposite to a load of me bollix, standard male resposne to question on merits of something.
entries.example: "Jayo Dublin have just won the all ireland how does it feel? Jayo: Grand"
entries.posh_english: Jayo Dublin have just won the all ireland how does it feel? Jayo: Grand. (Opposite to a load of me bollix, standard male resposne to question on merits of something.)

entries.definition: A yungfella up to no good, sometimes called a tipper or guyer.
entries.example: "Ya little gurrier! get ova here!"
entries.posh_english: You troublesome young scoundrel, come here this instant!

entries.definition: Like hiy, this word can be added arbitrarily at the end of a sentence to let the addressee know that you have completed it.
entries.example: "Jay I'm pure full hey, she'll do the nut when I get in hey!"
entries.posh_english: Goodness me, I am thoroughly stuffed, she shall throw a complete wobbly when I arrive home.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: The posterior opening of the alimentary canal. Used extensively, for example, means a kick in the posterior; and questions whether one pulled; finally, means someone will not do what you asked of them. Hoop is becoming a popular alternative to hole in modern Ireland.
entries.example:
"a boot in de hole"
"did you get your hole?"
"I will in my hole"
entries.posh_english: A swift propulsion to the rear.

entries.definition: Extremely. Can be used in positive as well as negative contexts.
entries.example: "He said I'd suck a sheep's eye through a hedge of nettles!!! Ah das horrid bad!!!"
entries.posh_english: He suggested I would perform a most unorthodox feat with a sheep. That is exceptionally dreadful!

entries.definition: Used to inform someone, if they do not keep their gob shut you will happily shut it for them.
entries.example:
"Hould yer whisht lads! Paddy is singing!"
How's yer livestock for a bullin'?
An invitation to a member of the opposite sex to engage in sexual intercourse.
"How's yer livestock for a bullin'? Wanna tip to Laytown for a bit of how's yer father?"
Moon
An exclamation of surprise at how peculiar something is. Similar to mental / mad.
"Naaavan won de foball??? Das moon!!!"
Motherless
Intoxicated to such an extent that either one forgets who their mother is or their mother disowns them, perhaps both.
"I was left motherless on the street last night!"
Praytays
A perennial plant of the Solanaceae otherwise known as potatoes. Praytays is an obvious bastardisation of the Gaelic for spuds, prátaí.
"Don't be givin' me de hairy eyeball (evil eye) now Mammy, just get me some of yer praytays, dare claaaass!!!"
entries.posh_english: Pray remain silent, gentlemen, as Mr Patrick is about to render a vocal performance!

entries.definition: A general Irish greeting believed to originate in the midlands.
entries.example:
"How's she cutting?"
"Like a serial killer!"
entries.posh_english: How are things progressing with you?

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: An affectionate term that can be used with complete strangers. Short for honey.
entries.example: "Want 'em battered or breadcrumbed hun?"
entries.posh_english: Would you prefer those fried in batter or coated in breadcrumbs, my dear?

entries.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck
entries.definition: An expression to emphasise that one is suffering from extreme hunger...
entries.example: "I'm so hungry I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck!"
entries.posh_english: Gentlemen I am so hungry I could devour the entire Kerry supporter off a low flying duck.

entries.phrase: I hope your next shite is a hedgehog
entries.definition: I hope the next time you go for a poo, it prick's you on the way out.
entries.example: "I hope your next shite is a hedgehog"
entries.posh_english: I hope your next visit to the lavatory is a hedgehog.

entries.definition: An expression used to bid farewell to you present company.
entries.example: "C'mere, I'll be away so before her indoors starts packing me things."
entries.posh_english: Listen here, I shall make my departure before my wife commences boxing up my belongings.

entries.definition: Sarcastic expression, used to tell someone that you will not perform the requested task.
entries.example: "Give you a gobblejob? I will yeah!"
entries.posh_english: Provide you with a sexual favour? I most certainly will not!

entries.definition: To be infatuated with someone.
entries.example: "Oh girls I'm soo in de boat with yer man dat works in the Four Lights, de Jimmy burgers he makes are just mighty!!!"
entries.posh_english: Oh girls, I am completely infatuated with that gentleman employed at the local grill, his culinary creations are simply splendid!

entries.definition: The toilet or W.C. Comes from Shakespeare's King Lear (II ii 74-6),
entries.example: "I shall tread this unbolted villain into mortar, and daub the wall of a jakes with him."
entries.posh_english: I shall trample this unprincipled scoundrel into mortar and plaster the lavatory walls with his remains.

entries.definition: An exclaimation of surprise.
entries.example: "Janey Mack, My shirt is black, what will I do for Sunday, I'll stay in bed and cover my head and not get up 'til Monday!"
entries.posh_english: Janey Mack my shirt is black what will I do for Sunday. I shall stay in bed and cover my head and not get up till Monday.

entries.definition: Expressions of surprise, probably to stop individuals from taking the Lord's name in vain.
entries.example: "Jaypers, did ya see dat?"
entries.posh_english: Good gracious me, did you witness that occurrence?

entries.definition: Irish pronunciation of Jesus.
entries.example: "Jaysus Christ!"
entries.posh_english: Good gracious me!

entries.definition: The individual as the object of his own reflective consciousness. The self. E.g.:
entries.example:
"Her jills is a tome beure."
"His jills et me sammich."
entries.posh_english: Her personal reflection is that of a remarkably imposing woman.

entries.definition: Physical pain, can also describe slagging.
entries.example: "De oul knee is givin me jip tonight!"
entries.posh_english: My aged knee is causing me a fearful amount of discomfort this evening!

entries.definition: Someone that is so ugly that you would have to tie a pork chop around their neck in order that the dog might play with them.
entries.example: "Whaddaya doin' sham, she's not a beore boy, she's kicked!"
entries.posh_english: What on earth are you doing, my good man, she is hardly a beauty, she is positively repulsive!

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: To be extremely tired. It comes from the original meaning of the word Knacker and not the modern derogatory term for a member of the travelling community.
entries.example: "I'm knackered after the weekend!"
entries.posh_english: I am utterly exhausted following the weekend's exertions.

entries.definition: Male genitalia - ballocks, bollox, bollix.
entries.example: "Me knackers are killing me after that ride last night"
entries.posh_english: My testicles are throbbing rather uncomfortably following last night's vigorous amorous congress.

entries.definition: A childish name for the male appendage, can be used in a similar way to gee to vehemently say no to somebody
entries.example: "I will in me corn on de cob!"
entries.posh_english: I shall do no such preposterous thing!

entries.definition: Small star shaped metal objects used in a game with the same name. Knucks were obtained from in the Ighrron Foundaghrree. Knucks can also be used as a euphemism for testicles.
entries.example: "Look at the big set of knucks on yer man!!!"
entries.posh_english: Pray cast your eyes upon the magnificent genitalia on that fellow!

entries.definition: The male / female naughty bit.
entries.example: "Arra I got a wile clatter in the Kooter!"
entries.posh_english: Good heavens, I received a tremendous thrashing about the nether regions.

entries.definition: Colloquial term for a female companion.
entries.example: "Giz a layarge bohhel offa de shellef boy, anna Ritz for de lack!"
entries.posh_english: Hand me a substantial vessel from the higher tier, old chap, and a pastry for the lady.

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition: Literally means penis, but can be used as an insult, or to affectionately refer to Cork people. It is a very flexible word and can be used in several situations.
entries.example: "Ye langer! Ye made me drink a langer-load and now I'm langers, ye langball!"
entries.posh_english: You absolute phallus! You compelled me to consume a penile quantity of liquor and now I am utterly plastered, you testicular vagabond!

entries.definition:
Very drunk.
Also: Cork people use this label to describe people they do not like. However, the rest of the country now use it to describe Cork people in general. It is synonymous with the word dickhead. Langer, literally translates as penis.
Also: To be drunk.
Also: Extremely drunk.
Also: Under the influence of alcohol.
entries.example:
"Was I drunk? Sure I was so langers, I fell in the door at home"
"You can hear dem langers coming a mile off."
"Lets get langered"
"..Woz I talkin t'you las' nigh' ... I was totally langered.."
"You were langers last night"
"Boys im langers!"
entries.posh_english: Was I drunk? Sure I was so inebriated I fell in the door at home.

entries.definition: Local pronunciation of the word lad. Led1: "Right hiy led, how's she cuttin' hiy?" Led2: "Full of de blade hiy!"
entries.example: "Right hi led, any craic?"
entries.posh_english: Greetings, my good chap, what is the latest gossip?

entries.definition: An expression used to describe the initiation of a passionate kiss, often without the permission of the gobbee (see Throw the head in, Louth).
entries.example: "I'm gonta bayte de head offa dat lang, did ye see de bollix lob de gob on me oul flower!"
entries.posh_english: I intend to dismantle that scoundrel, did you observe that ruffian kiss my mother!

entries.definition: Variation of Looder, which is an abbreviation of Liúdramán (Gaelic for a useless eejit).
entries.example: "The thunderin' loother dropped the ball again, I must be off me box putting him on!!!"
entries.posh_english: That clumsy dolt has dropped the sphere once more, I am completely at my wits end attempting to supervise him!

entries.definition: To kiss and perhaps do other stuff too.
entries.example:
Ma: "Did ye 'meet' yer man last night luv?"
Yungwan: "Ah, don't be a dirtbird ma!"
entries.posh_english: Did you snog that gentleman last night, darling?

entries.definition: A small bottle of a carbonated drink usually given free with a bag of chips and a battered sausage in chippers.
entries.example: "I'll have a pint and a mineral for the child"
entries.posh_english: I shall take a pint of ale and a carbonated beverage for the infant.

entries.definition: Something extremely good.
entries.example: "Did ya see his new yoke, 'tis mint!"
entries.posh_english: Have you clapped eyes on his new automobile? It is absolutely spiffing!

entries.definition: Male undergarments used to protect ones cacks from the dreaded skid-mark.
entries.example: "Ah forgot to do the paperwork and ended up with skid-marks on me monks!!!"
entries.posh_english: I quite forgot to attend to proper hygiene and consequently acquired fecal blemishes upon my underpants.

entries.definition: Irish pronunciation of mother. Often used in an insulting manner i.e.
entries.example: "Yer Mudder!"
entries.posh_english: Your maternal progenitor!

entries.definition:
Derogitory term for an individual insinuating a lack of self-determination.
Also: Dopey eejit.
Also: Idiot.
entries.example:
"Dat bleedin muppet couldn' score in a brothel"
"Hes an awful muppet"
"He's only a bleedin muppet!"
entries.posh_english: That bloody fool couldn't manage to kiss anyone in a bordello.

entries.definition: In the Name of Jaysus (exclamatory as opposed to reilgious use).
entries.example: "Namajaysus that heifer should be tied!"
entries.posh_english: Good gracious, that robust and unfavourably large lady should be secured!

entries.definition:
To have some nerve.
Also: Description of someone who will chance anything.
entries.example:
"He has a neck like a jockey's bollox"
"Yer man tried to get off with with some southside bird last night - way out of his league - he's a neck like a jockeys bollix"
entries.posh_english: He possesses a neck like a jockeys endowments.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: A child, generally one's own. Chizzlers is another common term for same.
entries.example:
Bridie: "Any nippers on de way yet Maggie?"
Maggie: "Go ask me arse!"
entries.posh_english: Any little urchins on the horizon yet, Margaret?

entries.definition: When a Leitrim person is asked something of a sensitive nature you will get this response.
entries.example:
Garda: "Can you elaborate on the situation?"
Local: "No commint."
entries.posh_english: Could you elaborate upon the circumstances?

entries.definition: This adjective doesn't have a real meaning, when you hear it being used just nod you're head in agreement. Possible variant of ohjuss (see Donegal).
entries.example: "Thawt was a nogeous sermon Fawder gave!"
entries.posh_english: That was a singularly tedious homily the vicar delivered.

entries.definition: The act of kissing the head off someone.
entries.example:
"I caught you nucking de head offa some tome beek... Fair play feenog!"
Note: Nuck literally translates as head and is used in many circumstances. For example: off their nuck (crazy), pig's nuck (ugly head), upside down nuck (bald man with a beard), crusty nuck (of new age tendencies), gugg nuck (baldy head), froshty nuck (pale face), turbo nuck (huge head), bird nuck (big nose) etc.
entries.posh_english: I observed you exchanging saliva with some rather unusual chap. Well played, old fellow!

entries.definition: Guttural war chant shouted at Portlaoise football matches.
entries.example: "On d'TOOOOWWWWWWNNNNN!"
entries.posh_english: Let us advance toward the town centre with considerable gusto!

entries.definition: An expression of agreement
entries.example: "On de ball boy, spot on no bodder!"
entries.posh_english: Spot on, dear boy, absolutely no trouble at all!

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition: Something that is great. Can mean gorgeous if referring to an individual.
entries.example: "You're on'y massiff ye ri-yed ye!"
entries.posh_english: You are remarkably attractive, you gorgeous creature!

entries.definition: Term used to describe a girlfriend or female spouse... can refer to ones mother in other counties which can lead to serious confusion. Oul Fella means dad, Oul Pair means parents and Oul Stock means friend.
entries.example:
Rebel: "Did ya shift yer oul doll last night?"
Monaghan man: "Yer sick ye dirty langer!"
entries.posh_english: Did you engage in nocturnal romance with your good lady wife last evening?

entries.definition: The armpit. If one smelled like a Donkey's oxter, they would be quite smelly indeed.
entries.example: "Smell of burger off your oxter"
entries.posh_english: There is a distinct aroma of charred beef emanating from your armpit.

entries.definition: Creamed mashed potato for babies.
entries.example: "I must make pandie for de peteen ban."
entries.posh_english: I must prepare some creamed potatoes for the little darling.

entries.definition: Colloquial designation for potatoes.
entries.example: "Pass de pirties 'pon de left hawnd saieede!"
entries.posh_english: Kindly pass the potatoes toward the left-hand side!

entries.definition: Adult term for urine, if one goes on the piss one is heading out for a few beverages with their friends. In the USA pissed means annoyed, however in Ireland it means drunk.
entries.example: "I have too much drink taken and need to go for a piss"
entries.posh_english: I have consumed rather too much claret and must urgently visit the lavatory.

entries.definition: An edible tuber native to South America; a staple food of Ireland, potatoes.
entries.example: "Gimme de pitters quick hiy, I'm so hungry I'd ate the scabby leg off a septic leper!"
entries.posh_english: Hand over the tubers immediately, for I am so famished I could eat an invalid.

entries.definition: What Wexford people call people from Kilkenny when vexed.
entries.example: "Onda model, let's bayte dem powderpissers."
entries.posh_english: Come along then, let us trounce those uncouth agricultural fellows.

entries.definition: A cupboard. One puts delph (plates, cups and saucers) in a press.
entries.example: "Get the blaas outa the press for me."
entries.posh_english: Retrieve the breakfast rolls from the larder for me.

entries.definition: Really/very.
entries.example: "Pure daycint biy"
entries.posh_english: He is a really quite decent fellow.

entries.definition:
Real, really, very much so.
Also: Used to exaggerate certain words.
entries.example:
"That guy is a pure fool."
"He is pure mad"
entries.posh_english: That fellow is a complete fool.

entries.definition: Totally; completely.
entries.example: "I was pure steaming last night"
entries.posh_english: I was completely steaming last night.

entries.definition: Used to describe something or some action in a praiseworthy sense.
entries.example: "She's looking quaran deadly dressed that well tonight. She's a real skeet."
entries.posh_english: She is looking quite excellent dressed so well this evening. She is a real beauty.

entries.definition: Quite, somewhat of.
entries.example: "Aye, he's a quare geg alright"
entries.posh_english: Indeed, he is quite an amusing character.

entries.definition:
Very or extremely.
Also: Strange.
entries.example:
"Kilkenny are quare bad a hurlin"
"That fella is quare fine!"
"Anythin Quare?"
entries.posh_english: The gentlemen of Kilkenny exhibit a most lamentable proficiency in the game of hurling.

entries.definition:
Used instead of really or very when describing something.
Also: An alternative word for very.
Also: Another meaning for very or unuasl.
entries.example:
"Those rissoles are quaar tasty"
"That's quar funny lads"
"Its quare cold out."
entries.posh_english: Those spice burgers are exceptionally palatable.

entries.definition: Suspicious character.
entries.example: "Keep your eye on that feen, he's a right queer hawk."
entries.posh_english: Keep your eye on that fellow he is a distinctly suspicious character.

entries.definition: Used to emphasise a word's importance..
entries.example: "Das quare ill boy, kicking him in de punnet like dah fer nahin."
entries.posh_english: That is particularly severe, my good fellow, applying physical violence to his groin in that unwarranted fashion.

entries.definition: Yet another word for the female private bit.
entries.example: "I'd love a bit of quim tonight"
entries.posh_english: I should rather fancy some feminine intimacy this evening.

entries.definition: A large, illuminous (sic), pink, meat-like sausage of unknown origin, otherwise known as luncheon sausage. Some say it is of a supernatural or extraterrestrial origin given its unusual colour and taste. Waterford locals believe it to be the original and best filling for blaas. Also goes by the name baloney in the West.
entries.example: "I loves red lead in me blaa."
entries.posh_english: I derive immense pleasure from consuming processed luncheon meat within my crusty bread roll.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: A goodlooking person.
entries.example: "Ye'r man is some ride"
entries.posh_english: That gentleman there is some remarkably handsome fellow.

entries.definition:
Really good looking girl or boy.
Also: (N.) A very attractive, sexually appealing individual. (v.) Have sex with, esp. as dominant partner.
entries.example:
"Yer man's a ride over there..."
"Commonly used to comment on facebook/bebo pictures: omg RIDEE!"
"...I'll ride the swiss roll offa you, ya little ride ya."
entries.posh_english: That gentleman over there is strikingly attractive.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: In most counties this term means an extremely attraction person with a huge amount of sex appeal, however, in Roscommon, along with the general meaning it can also mean a sound person or something that was very enjoyable.
entries.example: "Well ride, yer man I met after we had dat ride of a burger was some ride!!!"
entries.posh_english: Greetings, my attractive fellow, the gentleman I encountered after we shared that remarkably splendid hamburger was quite something!

entries.definition: Potato cakes mixed with indigenous herbs and spices, battered or bread-crumbed and deep-fried before serving with a large chip (potato fries). Called a spice burger elsewhere.
entries.example: "Don't forget ta puh loadsa salt 'n' vinegar on me Rissoles hun!!!"
entries.posh_english: Do make sure to apply a generous quantity of salt and vinegar to my potato cakes, darling.

entries.definition: Local pronunciation of roll meaning to knock someone over with a shoulder or a punch.
entries.example: "Jaysus dat lad is quare hardy, he'd rowl ya handy I'd say!"
entries.posh_english: Good heavens that fellow is remarkably robust, he would floor you quite easily I daresay.

entries.definition: An eraser, usually found in a pencil case with rulers and toppers. Can also mean condom (see Jonnies).
entries.example: "Dont forget youe rubber if you want to have your hole"
entries.posh_english: Do not forget your prophylactic sheath should you wish to engage in commerce.

entries.definition: An adjective to describe someone that is one can short of a six pack or nuts (in a good way).
entries.example:
Frank: "I said to her, 'I betcha 5 euro I can feel yer Prátaís without touching them' and she said 'yeah right' so I grabbed them and gave her the fiver!!!?"
Quentin: "You are wan rulya feen!"
entries.posh_english: You are a thoroughly unorthodox character.

entries.definition: A childish term for one's scrotum. Nob and sack go hand in hand. A less offensive term for one's sack is the Gaelic for balls, líathróidí. is a vulgar phrase often used today in place of
entries.example:
"Bite me sack!"
"Feck off!"
entries.posh_english: Masticate my scrotum!

entries.definition: Over description of event,thing or person.
entries.example: "She has savage pair a legs on her!"
entries.posh_english: She has a remarkably fine pair of legs on her.

entries.definition:
Great.
Also: Sumtin ya like.
entries.example:
"That was a savage nyom!"
"That car is savage"
entries.posh_english: That was an absolutely splendid meal.

entries.definition: It was deadly.
entries.example: "Aw man it was savage!"
entries.posh_english: My word, old chap, that was remarkably splendid!

entries.definition:
Mate, Buddy, Friend.
Also: A friend.
Also: Peron.
entries.example:
"Fair play tya sham' or 'Aboy the sham"
"Howya sham, I hear ye got a new set o' tackies"
"Well sham...whats the story?"
entries.posh_english: Splendid performance, my good companion.

entries.definition: A human male. Often associated with Tuam.
entries.example:
"Hey sham, can I have butts on dat fag? I'm hangin' for a few puffs... I haven't had a drag in yonks!"
N.B. One must take care asking for butts on a fag as it may be confused with a request for homosexual intimacy.
entries.posh_english: I say, old chap, might I trouble you for a light on this cigarette, as I am absolutely gagging for a puff.

entries.definition: Sham. A well known town drunk in killarney and well know lady killer.
entries.example: "Walking down the street, you see him. 'ALRIGHT SHAM!'"
entries.posh_english: Good day to you, champion of the town!

entries.definition: Any of numerous aquatic (Perry Winkle) or terrestrial (Snail) molluscs, typically having a spirally coiled shell. A Snail.
entries.example: "Shellaky Shellakybooky, stick out your horns and see the white lady coming to call you."
entries.posh_english: Little mollusc of the garden, extend your sensory tentacles and observe the aristocratic lady approaching for a visit.

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition: Generally means to enthusiastically kiss a member of the opposite sex. Can mean quite a bit more than kissing in some counties. Examples of other words for shifting such as meetin' and tippin' can be found throughout this book.
entries.example: "I'd love to shift her"
entries.posh_english: I should very much like to engage in a passionate embrace with her.

entries.definition: To french kiss someone.
entries.example: "Awww here will you go round the back of the shed with fintan whelan and shift him"
entries.posh_english: Will you go round the back of the shed with Fintan Whelan and exchange a French kiss with him.

entries.definition: French Kiss-
entries.example: "Aboy, you shift her last night?"
entries.posh_english: I say, did you French kiss her last night?

entries.definition: An expression used to call in the heifers in for an oul milkin'.
entries.example: "Sook Sook, c'mere ye stupid aminals (sic)."
entries.posh_english: Come along, you rather dim livestock.

entries.definition: A person who is liked because they do nice things for their friends
entries.example: "Paddy gave me a loand of hees car. He's sound as a trout!"
entries.posh_english: Patrick kindly lent me his motorcar. He is an exceptionally agreeable sort!

entries.definition:
Decent/dead on.
Also: It may be used as an affirmative, or to describe someone in a positive manner.
Also: Dat fella is good fella good 2 you.
entries.example:
"He's sound' or can also be used to describe how you feel - 'sound"
"That's sound/ Oh ya she's sound"
"Aw wman he gave me few euro there hes pure sound"
entries.posh_english: He is a thoroughly decent sort.

entries.definition: Very good, or nice person.
entries.example: "Thanks for the cigarette, you're a sound man"
entries.posh_english: Many thanks for the cigarette, you are a thoroughly decent fellow.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: It means the same as dead on. when someone is fun, no hassle etc.
entries.example:
Kevin: "Do u no niall?"
Sean: "Aw yeah, he's dead on."
entries.posh_english: Ah yes, he is thoroughly agreeable company.

entries.definition: An expression of delight, meaning brilliant. Alternatives are "Belter" and "Magic hiy!"
entries.example: "Sweet to the beat, I'll meet yousens later an down baiee wulwufs! Belter! Magic hiy!"
entries.posh_english: Splendid news, I shall rendezvous with you gentlemen later.

entries.definition: Running shoes. The expression "I took tackie after him," means "I chased him".
entries.example: "Look at de tackies on yer man, he must be from Stab-a-jax!"
entries.posh_english: Observe the athletic footwear upon that fellow, he clearly hails from rather robust origins.

entries.definition: Any variety of savoury packet snack. Comes from a local pronunciation of the popular brand of Irish potato crisp (chip if yer a yank) called Tayto. If you're from Laois or Offaly, "a packeh of Tayho," could mean Skips, Meanies, Chickatees, Rancheros, Monster / Mighty Munch, Snax, Tayto crisps themselves or any other savoury packet snack for that matter!!!
entries.example: "I may go lad, I'm mowlin' for a few ice creams (pints of stout) anna Tayho sammich."
entries.posh_english: I may accompany you my good man, as I am positively pining for several sherries and a potato crisp sandwich.

entries.definition: Cork people believe they live in their own independent state... It suits the rest of the country though as it keeps the weird accent from spreading too far past the boundary.
entries.example: "Where you from boy? The People's Republic of Cork, boy? Where else?"
entries.posh_english: From whence do you hail, my good fellow? The sovereign commonwealth of our southern county, obviously. Where else could one possibly originate?

entries.definition: Generally used to describe someone who is not the sharpest pencil in the box, but can also be used to describe someone with a short fuse.
entries.example: "Yer mawn yonder is fiersche thick, he keeps getting thick with me for callin' him a cream bun!"
entries.posh_english: That fellow over there is exceedingly dense, and he continually loses his temper with me for calling him a pastry.

entries.definition: Distinguished by qualities which excite admiration; splendid; shining; as, brilliant talents.
entries.example: "We had a tome night last night in the Gypo."
entries.posh_english: We had a splendid evening yesterday at the public house.

entries.definition: Another word for an eejit. Spanner and spoon are other alternatives.
entries.example: "Yurn some tool"
entries.posh_english: You are rather a monumental fool.

entries.definition:
Fool.
Also: See misterman's submission.
Also: Penis.
Also: Term used to insult a person.
entries.example:
"You're some feckin tool you are"
"That misterman is nobody's tool"
"Hes a tool that fella"
entries.posh_english: You are a remarkably foolish bounder.

entries.definition: Stupid Person.
entries.example: "Dat fella's an absolute tool"
entries.posh_english: That particular gentleman is an absolute fool.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition:
See misterman in limerick's entry.
Also: A fool of a man.
entries.example:
"That mrman is nobody's tool"
"That lad is some tool"
entries.posh_english: That gentleman is nobody's fool.

entries.definition: Simple replacement words for unbelievable.
entries.example: "Lads de sesh was unreal last night, I'm as sick as de plane to Lourdes dis morning an' I have an unnatural headache!"
entries.posh_english: Good fellows, the nocturnal carousing was quite extraordinary last evening.

entries.definition: A confusing phrase shouted by Down fans at GAA matches, whether supporting the Ardsmen (Hurling) or Mournmen (Football).
entries.example: "I cawn't wait for de tay n' sammiches come Sunday!!! Up Down Hiy!"
entries.posh_english: I am eagerly anticipating the tea and sandwiches on Sunday.

entries.definition: A joyous outburst, may be heard when the team being supported scores a goal.
entries.example:
"Up she flew biys...
...and the cock flattened her!"
entries.posh_english: Up she went, my good chaps.

entries.definition: Nickname for the Mercy Convent. Yungfella1: "Dem youngwans in de Virgin Megastore are a pack of pure dry, moany, wreck de heads." Yungfella2, in agreement, mutters: "Ahoii!"
entries.example: "Shopping at the Virgin Megastore has never been easier now the points have dropped for the courses there."
entries.posh_english: Attending that religious seminary has never been more straightforward now the entrance requirements have decreased for the programmes there.

entries.definition: An cantankerous old woman, generally quite large, packing a serious punch.
entries.example: "Yer wan is some oul wagon, I asked her could I feed the seagulls and she lifted me out of it!"
entries.posh_english: That woman is a formidable battle-axe, I merely inquired about feeding the gulls and she physically ejected me from the premises!

entries.definition: A greeting used in many counties throughout the country often used in conjunction with or
entries.example:
"girl"
"boy."
entries.posh_english: Good day, young lady.

entries.definition: Expression to tell someone to desist from speaking and begin to listen with intention.
entries.example:
"Whisht, look at yer wan..."
"I wouldn't touch her with yours Paddy!"
entries.posh_english: Hush now, do observe that peculiar creature yonder.

related.phrase: Beef to the heel like a Mullingar heifer

entries.definition: To be knowledgeable about something.
entries.example: "Are ye wide sham?"
entries.posh_english: Are you fully cognizant of the situation, old sport?

entries.definition: Very bad or terrible.
entries.example: "Look out de windy, 'tis a wile bawd day!"
entries.posh_english: Pray gaze out of the casement, it is a rather frightful day!

entries.definition: An entanglement in the "barse" region i.e. the area between one's balls and arse.
entries.example: "Go wash dem wilnots off of the baieegs of yer barse!"
entries.posh_english: Be so good as to eradicate those perspiration clusters from your perineum!

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition: An expression of friendly banter. Can be extended with the word boot as in"
entries.example: "G'way outa dat ya hoor's boot ya!"
entries.posh_english: Do jog on, you delightful bounder!

entries.definition: Hand to hand combat.
entries.example: "Do ya want yer go boy? I'll give ye a baytin' by de clock tower at tenna past 4! By the way, if I'm late feel free tew start without me!"
entries.posh_english: Would you fancy a round of fisticuffs? I shall give you a proper drubbing by the clock tower at ten past four!

related.phrase: I'd ate de bollix offa low flyin' duck

entries.definition:
A word describing a commerically savvy human (usually male).
Also: An allusion to a male known to both parties.
entries.example:
"Did you hear yermann from Aerlingus bought Man Utd for ten grand?"
"I saw yer man Colin last night in da pub last night he was stocious"
entries.posh_english: Have you heard that the commercially astute fellow from Aer Lingus acquired Manchester United for a mere ten thousand pounds?

entries.definition: Used at the start of every sentence. As you move northwards "Yerrah" becomes "Erra" until it becomes "Arra" north of Clare.
entries.example:
"Yerra, 'twas hard (cold) today so I brought me flashk of tay with me to get a gabhal of turf from de bog, but I forgot the feckin' ponny (enamel cup) to put it in! Ah pants!"
A Kerryman Joke (or two)
What would the Kerry section be without a couple of cringeworthy Kerryman jokes...
What do they call 'Pop Idol' in Kerry?
Diddly Idol!
Did you hear about the Kerryman who thought he was gay?
He preferred hurling to football!
entries.posh_english: Well now, it was rather chilly today so I brought my receptacle of infusion to harvest a spadeful of peat from the mire, but alas I forgot the tin vessel to contain it. Oh botheration!

entries.definition: An arbitrary object, can also be used to refer to a person as in,
entries.example: "Ye mad yoke!"
entries.posh_english: You delightfully eccentric specimen!

entries.definition: A mode of transport, usually a fancy tractor.
entries.example: "That's a quare yoke there"
entries.posh_english: That is a rather peculiar agricultural vehicle parked over there.

entries.definition: A quick way of calling attention to something you can't think of the name of.
entries.example: "Hand me that yoke, would ya? Or, ya have ta attach this yoke to it before it works."
entries.posh_english: Would you kindly hand me that implement? Or alternatively, you must attach this implement to it before it functions.

entries.definition: A word used to name something instead of its proper name.
entries.example: "Pass me that yoke (pass me that hammer)"
entries.posh_english: Hand me that implement.

entries.definition:
A thing, also slang for Ecstacy.
Also: An object,or a person.
Also: Ecstasy.
Also: Ecstacy.
Also: An object.
entries.example:
"Where the remote? those kids are after hiding the fecking yoke again."
"Got any yokes? what are they? doves?"
"That yoke is broke,pass me that yoke, she's ayoke"
"Have ya any yokes lads"
"Any yokes lads? / whats that yoke?"
entries.posh_english: Where on earth is the remote control? Those children have concealed the wretched object yet again.
